name: Cultural Landscape and Archaeological Remains of the Bamiyan Valley
description: In Afghanistan's Bamiyan Valley, about 130 km northwest of Kabul and 2,500 m up, honeycombed sandstone cliffs hold Buddhist monasteries and painted caves from the Silk Road era. Two giant Buddhas, 38 m and 55 m tall, were carved here in the 6th–7th centuries. The Taliban destroyed them in 2001, leaving vast empty niches. Fortresses from the Islamic period also survive.
